title: Seeded extraction with constant total entropy loss
formal:
Do there exist an explicit family of ordinary seeded extractors and absolute constants \(C,\Delta\in\mathbb N\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge2\) and \(0\le k\le n\), the family supplies a function
\[\operatorname{Ext}_{n,k}:\{0,1\}^{n}\times\{0,1\}^{d(n,k)}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{m(n,k)}\]
with
\[d(n,k)\le C\lceil\log_2 n\rceil,\qquad 0\le k+d(n,k)-m(n,k)\le\Delta,\]
and, for every distribution \(X\) on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\) with min-entropy at least \(k\),
\[\operatorname{TV}\bigl(\operatorname{Ext}_{n,k}(X,U_{d(n,k)}),U_{m(n,k)}\bigr)\le1/100?\]
The seed is uniform and independent of \(X\). Explicitness means uniform deterministic evaluation in time polynomial in \(n\), with the same algorithm and polynomial for all \(n,k\). This is the constant-total-entropy-loss question in Vadhan's Open Problem 6.41.
why: This asks whether an efficient general randomness purifier can preserve all but a constant number of the available random bits while using only a logarithmic seed. In applications that enumerate seeds or pay exponentially for entropy loss, the additive loss determines a multiplicative cost. Resolving the question would distinguish information-theoretic feasibility from the achievable efficiency of explicit extraction.
status_note: Open Problem 6.41 and the surrounding parameter table were read directly on 2026-09-14. A bounded later-literature search and inspection of Doron–Ribeiro version 2 (9 February 2026) found no matching uniform logarithmic-seed, constant-total-loss construction or impossibility theorem. progress.text: Open Problem 6.41 asks for logarithmic seed length and output equal to source entropy plus seed length up to an additive constant, at error 0.01.

Doron and Ribeiro revise their short-seed extractor construction and its nearly-linear evaluation bounds. The checked theorem retains a constant-fraction output guarantee, with preprocessing qualifications, rather than constant total entropy loss.

sentences: A seeded extractor combines an arbitrary weak random source with a short independent uniform seed.
This question asks for logarithmic seed length and an output losing at most a constant number of the combined available entropy bits.
The statistical error is fixed at one hundredth for every source meeting the min-entropy bound.
The entire family must be evaluated by one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, including any preprocessing.
Nonconstructive existence and recent faster constant-fraction extractors leave this specific combination of parameters unsettled in the checked sources.

definitions:
All lengths \(n,k,d,m\) are integers measured in bits, with \(d,m\ge0\), and logarithms have base two. For a finite random variable \(X\),
\[H_{\infty}(X)=-\log_2\max_x\Pr[X=x].\]
Thus the source promise is \(\Pr[X=x]\le2^{-k}\) for every \(n\)-bit string \(x\). The source may have arbitrary dependencies between its coordinates and need not be samplable by an efficient algorithm. The extractor receives a sample string, not a description of its distribution. \(U_t\) denotes the uniform distribution on all \(t\)-bit strings, including the unique empty string when \(t=0\). For distributions \(P,Q\) on the same finite set,
\[\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)=\tfrac12\sum_z|P(z)-Q(z)|.\]
The condition is statistical and quantifies over every promised source, with no computational restriction on a test of the output.

A family is explicit if there are two fixed deterministic multitape Turing machines and integers \(K,q\ge1\): a parameter machine on \((1^n,k)\), with \(k\) in binary, outputs \(d(n,k),m(n,k)\) in binary; an evaluation machine on \((1^n,k,x,y)\) outputs the entire \(m(n,k)\)-bit string. Both halt within \(K(n+1)^q\) steps on all valid inputs. All preprocessing and output writing are counted. There is no advice, oracle, randomized construction or length-dependent table supplied for free. The machines, \(C,\Delta,K,q\) are chosen before \(n,k\) and before the source distribution.

Total entropy loss means \(k+d-m\): it counts the source's guaranteed entropy together with all perfect seed bits consumed. This ordinary extractor requirement concerns the output distribution alone. It does not require that the output remain uniform when the seed is separately disclosed. A strong extractor, whose output is uniform jointly with a disclosed seed, may be converted to an ordinary one by including its seed in the total output, but those seed bits must then be counted in \(m\). The convention \(m\le k+d\) is harmless output truncation for this error level. Integer entropy thresholds suffice for the stated additive-constant target; rounding down a real threshold changes the loss by less than one bit.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed uniform construction claim. A positive answer must specify the algorithms and universal constants and prove the extraction guarantee, logarithmic seed bound, constant total loss and polynomial evaluation time throughout the parameter domain. A negative answer must rule out every such uniform family. An existence proof without efficient evaluation, a loss growing with \(n\) or \(k\), or an output bound that ignores consumed seed entropy does not meet the criterion.

context_blocks.text: The probabilistic existence bounds in the source permit logarithmic seed length and constant total entropy loss at fixed error. The obstacle in this question is a single efficiently evaluable construction, rather than the existence of a suitable finite table for each pair of parameters.

Vadhan contrasts logarithmic-seed constructions that extract a constant fraction of the source entropy with constructions extracting all but a constant number of source bits using a polylogarithmic seed. Neither parameter guarantee by itself gives \(m\ge k+d-O(1)\) with \(d=O(\log n)\).

The 2026 revised Doron–Ribeiro paper improves evaluation time for short-seed strong extractors. Its Theorem 1 gives \(m\ge(1-\eta)k\) and \(d=O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\) for fixed \(\eta>0\), with stated entropy and preprocessing conditions. Even after counting the seed as part of an ordinary output, the theorem allows a loss proportional to \(k\); it does not establish the constant-loss target.

The adjacent seed-length question TCS-1016 instead fixes the leading coefficient of the logarithm and allows only a constant fraction of source entropy as output. These two additive-precision questions have different required guarantees.
